lines.trans: Open the flap gently, Nour; that little envelope has waited patiently since May.
Inside is a folded ivory note card written in the same crisp mapmaker ink!
Please read every word aloud for us, Nour.
Dear Friends of Jasmine Street, if you are sitting on our favourite park bench today...
Then Room Nine has opened its green shutters to the neighbourhood once more!
Listen to the next line: Thirty summers ago, five friends made a Saturday promise.
What promise did my professor and the courtyard crew make back then, Nour?
To hang lanterns from the red-star balcony and share berry almond cake again!
Oh, how lovely—and is there a postscript at the bottom of the card?
Look: Watch your front-desk mail this week, because I keep my promises!
Wait—he already mailed that first postcard from abroad two weeks ago!
What if a second message arrived at Jasmine Courtyard while we were out walking?!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفتح, بيفتح).

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
Oh, the door finally opened!

meanings.note: The word 'طية' (el-Tayye) means 'the flap'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: افتحي الطية بلطف يا نور؛ هالمغلف الصغير استنى بصبر من شهر خمسة.
examples.trans: Open the flap gently, Nour; that little envelope has waited patiently since May.
This is طية.

meanings.note: Form II verb (lattaf): ألطف الجو ('lighten the tense mood').

examples.trans: She told a joke to lighten the mood.
A kind word softens the atmosphere.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Appears in صباح النور ('morning of light', the standard reply to صباح الخير) and نور الشمس ('sunlight').

examples.trans: Good morning and welcome!
We read the card in the sunlight.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مغلفات.

examples.trans: There is a white envelope taped to the door.
We opened the thick envelope calmly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: صغيرة, plural: صغار).

examples.trans: We found a little wooden train in the bag.
There are two small streets on the left.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستنى, بيستنى).

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Thank you very much for your patience with us.
Patience is the key to relief.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شهور.

examples.trans: That was the best sleep in a month!
The contract renews at the start of next month.

meanings.note: Numeral 'five'; short form خمس (khams) before a plural noun (خمس دقايق 'five minutes').

examples.trans: It is five to twelve.

examples.text: الدكان على بعد خمس دقايق مشي.
examples.trans: The shop is five minutes' walk away.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('inside the bag') and standalone ('inside').

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
The water is flowing inside!

في.gloss: there is; there are; is there?

meanings.en: there is; there are; is there?
meanings.note: Spoken Levantine existential word ('there is / there are'); negated as ما في ('there is no / there are no').

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كروت.

examples.text: بعتتله كرت بريد قصير الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: I sent him a short postcard last week.
I recognised his neat handwriting on the card right away.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ملاحظات.

examples.trans: He wrote all the street notes in the notebook.
Thank you for that helpful observation.

meanings.note: The word 'عاجي' (3aaji) means 'ivory'. It is a common adj in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: جوا في كرت ملاحظات عاجي مطوي ومكتوب بنفس حبر رسام الخرايط الواضح!
examples.trans: Inside is a folded ivory note card written in the same crisp mapmaker ink!
This is عاجي.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مطوية, plural: مطويين).

examples.trans: We found an old folded map in the box.

examples.text: في ورقة تانية مطوية ورا الإشعار.
examples.trans: There is a second folded sheet behind the notice.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مكتوبة, plural: مكتوبين).

examples.trans: What is written in the letter, Nour?
Our two names are still written in pencil.

meanings.note: Unvocalised نفس covers nafas ('breath': خد نفس عميق take a deep breath) and nafs ('same': نفس الشي the same thing).

examples.trans: Take a deep breath and calm down.
We took the exact same bus in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أحبار.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in blue ink.
The ink pen is on the desk.

meanings.note: The word 'رسام' (rassaam) means 'mapmaker'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ليش رسام الخرايط رسم نجمة حمرا على بلكونة ساحتنا اللي فوق؟!
examples.trans: Why did the mapmaker paint a red star on our upstairs courtyard balcony?!
This is رسام.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: خرايط.

examples.trans: Look at the folded map inside the box.
We drew a small map of the street.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واضحة, plural: واضحين).

examples.trans: A sincere, clear sentence from the heart.
The address is clear on the card.

meanings.note: Introduces polite requests (لو سمحت 'if you please') and hypothetical conditions ('if').

examples.trans: Take the guesthouse number, please.
Even if he is a little late, wait for him.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسمح, بيسمح).

examples.trans: Take the guesthouse number, please.
Allow me to pour the orange juice.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقرأ, بيقرأ).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Did you read the second page clipped underneath?

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun كل means 'every' (كل يوم 'every day'); before a definite noun it means 'all / the whole' (كل الأسبوع 'all week').

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أصوات.

examples.trans: I heard the sound of rain on the window.
His voice is calm and polite on the phone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عالية, plural: عاليين).

examples.trans: What is that loud sound upstairs?
The wooden ceiling is high and sunny.

meanings.note: The word 'لـ' (لـ) means 'لـ'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: معها حق—أنا عم أعمل لفائف القرفة لفترة بعد الظهر لـ بيت الياسمين.
examples.trans: She is right—I am making the afternoon cinnamon rolls for Jasmine Courtyard.
This is لـ.

meanings.note: The word 'صديق' (aSdiqaa'i) means 'my friends'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أصدقائي الأعزاء بشارع شارع الياسمين، إذا قاعدين على مقعد الحديقة المفضل تبعنا اليوم...
examples.trans: Dear Friends of Jasmine Street, if you are sitting on our favourite park bench today...
This is صديق.

meanings.note: The word 'عزيز' (el-a3izzaa') means 'dear'. It is a common adj in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أصدقائي الأعزاء بشارع شارع الياسمين، إذا قاعدين على مقعد الحديقة المفضل تبعنا اليوم...
examples.trans: Dear Friends of Jasmine Street, if you are sitting on our favourite park bench today...
This is عزيز.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شوارع.

examples.trans: Our guesthouse is on a quiet street in central Amman.
There are old stone streets in the quarter.

meanings.note: The word 'الياسمين' (الياسمين) means 'الياسمين'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: شو هالصباح الحلو يوم السبت لمشية كنز بشارع شارع الياسمين!
examples.trans: What a glorious Saturday morning for a treasure walk down Jasmine Street!
This is الياسمين.

meanings.note: Everyday conditional word 'if' for real possibilities.

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

examples.text: إذا فتحنا الساحة الصبح، الجيران بيفرحوا.
examples.trans: If we open the courtyard in the morning, the neighbours will be delighted.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قاعدة, plural: قاعدين).

examples.trans: Who is sitting in our courtyard under the tree?
We are sitting having tea.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Noun of place from ق-ع-د ('to sit'); names the seat of a chair or a garden bench.

examples.text: ارفع مقعد الكرسي شوي عشان يطوي معك.
examples.trans: Lift the chair seat slightly so it folds for you.

examples.text: في مقعد خشب طويل تحت شجرة الساحة.
examples.trans: There is a long wooden bench under the courtyard tree.

meanings.note: The word 'حديقة' (la-hal-Hadeeqa) means 'to this park'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هينا وصلنا لبرج الساعة البلدي—والخيال بيأشر دغري لهالحديقة!
examples.trans: Here we are at the municipal clock tower—and the shadow points straight to this park!
This is حديقة.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مفضلة, plural: مفضلين).

examples.trans: This is my favourite cup for tea.

examples.text: كيكة الليمون هي الحلو المفضل عندهم.
examples.trans: Lemon cake is their favourite dessert.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian possessive word ('belonging to'); agrees in gender: تبع (m.), تبعت (f.), تبعون (pl.).

examples.text: اليوم آخر يوم بأسبوع التجربة تبعك.
examples.trans: Today is the last day of your trial week.
My brother's piano teacher!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أيام.

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!

meanings.note: The word 'معنى' (ma3naato) means 'its meaning (then)'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: معناته غرفة تسعة فتحت شبابيكها الخضرا للحارة كمان مرة!
examples.trans: Then Room Nine has opened its green shutters to the neighbourhood once more!
This is معنى.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: غرف.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Numeral 'nine'; short form تسع (tisa') before a plural noun (تسع دقايق 'nine minutes').

examples.trans: The quietness in the courtyard is nine out of ten!
She came back in just nine minutes!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شبابيك.

examples.trans: The window overlooks the courtyard tree.
We painted the wooden shutters in summer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خضرا, plural: خضر).

examples.trans: Pass beside the green pharmacy.
Put the green herbs on the eggs.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: حارات.

examples.trans: The shop is right here in our neighbourhood.
Old Amman neighbourhoods are peaceful.

كمان.gloss: also; too; again (كمان مرة once more)

meanings.en: also; too; again (كمان مرة once more)
meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for 'also, too, more' (كمان مرة 'one more time / again').

examples.text: التفكير السريع أنقذ الفطور كمان مرة!
examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast once again!
And I missed you too.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مرات.

examples.trans: The doorbell rang twice.
I read the letter three times.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسمع, بيسمع).

examples.trans: Did you hear the gate bell downstairs?
Inside the courtyard we hear the tree leaves.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سطور.

examples.trans: Read me the top line of the letter.
He wrote two short lines on the card.

meanings.note: Active participle of إجا ('to come'): means 'on the way / arriving' (جايين 'they are coming') and after a time noun 'next' (الأسبوع الجاي 'next week').

examples.trans: The guests are coming down the stairs now.
We will see you next week!

meanings.note: Means 'before' (قبل الفطور) and with a time span 'ago' (قبل ساعة 'an hour ago', قبل شوي 'just now').

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'thirty'.

examples.trans: They have given us thirty days in the letter.
The bill is thirty-eight dinars.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Evenings in Amman are pleasant in summer.
Our rent is paid until next summer.

meanings.note: The word 'خمس' (khams) means 'five'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: اسمعوا السطر الجاي: قبل تلاتين صيف، خمس أصحاب قطعوا وعد يوم السبت.
examples.trans: Listen to the next line: Thirty summers ago, five friends made a Saturday promise.
This is خمس.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صحاب.

examples.trans: Who is the owner of the blue suitcase?
We became friends from the first day.

meanings.note: The word 'قطع' (qaTa3oo) means 'they cut/made'. It is a common verb in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: اسمعوا السطر الجاي: قبل تلاتين صيف، خمس أصحاب قطعوا وعد يوم السبت.
examples.trans: Listen to the next line: Thirty summers ago, five friends made a Saturday promise.
This is قطع.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: وعود.

examples.trans: We will come next week, promise!
He kept his promise and arrived on time.

meanings.note: The word 'سبت' (el-sabt) means 'Saturday'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: شو هالصباح الحلو يوم السبت لمشية كنز بشارع شارع الياسمين!
examples.trans: What a glorious Saturday morning for a treasure walk down Jasmine Street!
This is سبت.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine question word for 'what?'.

examples.trans: What is that sound?
What is written on the sheet, Rami?

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Jordanian relative pronoun ('who, which, that') for any gender or number.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: The word 'دكتور' (duktoori) means 'my professor'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: شو الوعد اللي قطعه دكتوري وشلة الساحة هداك الوقت يا نور؟
examples.trans: What promise did my professor and the courtyard crew make back then, Nour?
This is دكتور.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a tight-knit school clique (شلتها 'her clique').

examples.trans: The whole school knows Layan's clique.
I sat with my friend group at recess.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian distal demonstrative ('that over there / that past...'); feminine هديك (hadiik), plural هدولاك.

examples.text: بتذكر هداك الربيع لما فتحنا النزل؟
examples.trans: Do you remember that spring when we opened the inn?

examples.text: حط الصندوق على هداك الرف العالي.
examples.trans: Put the box on that high shelf.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أوقات.

examples.trans: Old pipes take time to warm up.
You arrived right on time.

meanings.note: Form I intransitive verb ('iliq / byi'laq) meaning 'get stuck or jammed'; contrast transitive علّق ('hang up / jam').

examples.text: المفتاح القديم علق بالقفل من الصدا.
examples.trans: The old key got stuck in the lock from rust.
The sheet of paper got wedged behind the wooden rest.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فوانيس.

examples.trans: The golden lanterns are lit in the courtyard.
We hung a brass lantern by the entrance.

meanings.note: The word 'بلكونة' (balkoonet) means 'balcony'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: وشوفوا لفوق على بلكونة الساحة الخشبية بالطابق التاني—نجمة حمرا فاقعة مرسومة!
examples.trans: And look up on the second-floor wooden courtyard balcony—a bright red painted star!
This is بلكونة.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: نجوم.

examples.trans: The sky is clear and full of stars tonight.
The guesthouse service deserves five stars!

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine حمرا (hamra); شاي أحمر means black tea.

examples.trans: Would you like coffee or black tea?
There is a red ribbon on my suitcase.

meanings.note: The word 'شارك' (w-nshaarek) means 'and we share'. It is a common verb in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: نعلق فوانيس من بلكونة النجمة الحمرا ونشارك كيكة اللوز والتوت كمان مرة!
examples.trans: To hang lanterns from the red-star balcony and share berry almond cake again!
This is شارك.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: كيكات.

examples.text: كيكة الليمون الصفرا طلعت من الفرن.
examples.trans: The yellow lemon cake came out of the oven.
We sliced the cake into six equal pieces.

meanings.note: Collective noun for almonds (singulative لوزة).

examples.text: ريحة اللوز المحمص طالعة من فرن سلمى.
examples.trans: The aroma of toasted almonds is drifting out of Salma's oven.

examples.text: قشرة اللوز بتعطي تارت الليمون قرمشة طيبة.
examples.trans: An almond crust gives the lemon tart a delicious crunch.

meanings.note: The word 'توت' (wel-toot) means 'and berries'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: نعلق فوانيس من بلكونة النجمة الحمرا ونشارك كيكة اللوز والتوت كمان مرة!
examples.trans: To hang lanterns from the red-star balcony and share berry almond cake again!
This is توت.

meanings.note: The word 'الله' (alla) means 'God'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: يا الله شو حلو—وفي ملاحظة بالآخر بكعب الكرت؟
examples.trans: Oh, how lovely—and is there a postscript at the bottom of the card?
This is الله.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: حلوة, plural: حلوين).

examples.trans: The strawberry jam is sweet and tasty.
The sweater looks lovely and warm.

meanings.note: Placed directly before an indefinite noun without ال- to mean 'the last' (آخر يوم 'the last day', آخر الساحة 'the far end of the courtyard').

examples.trans: The attic room is at the end of the floor.
Today is the last day of the week.

meanings.note: Names the heel of a foot or shoe (كعب القدم / كعب الحذاء).

examples.text: زحلق كعب حذائي عن حرف الطبلية الواطية.
examples.trans: The heel of my shoe slipped off the edge of the low stool.

examples.text: اسندي كعبك عالوسادة الطرية عشان ترتاح رجلك.
examples.trans: Rest your heel on the soft cushion so your foot can relax.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Form III verb meaning 'keep a close eye on an oven, timer, or process'.

examples.text: أبو طارق بيراقب درجة حرارة الفرن والمؤقت.
examples.trans: Abu Tariq watches the oven temperature and the timer.

examples.text: أنا براقب من الكرسي وبعطيكم التعليمات.
examples.trans: I'll watch from the chair and give you instructions.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: A postcard arrived in the morning.
The postman rang the bell.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مكاتب.

examples.trans: The keys are on the reception desk.
The wooden desk under the window is wide.

meanings.note: Relational adjective from أمام ('in front of'): الغرفة الأمامية / الباب الأمامي.

examples.text: علقنا اللوحة الجديدة جنب البوابة الأمامية.
examples.trans: We hung the new sign beside the front gate.
The front windows look straight out onto the lane.

meanings.note: The word 'اسبوع' (hal-usboo3) means 'this week'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: شوفوا: راقبوا بريد المكتب الأمامي هالاسبوع، لأني بوفي بوعودي!
examples.trans: Look: Watch your front-desk mail this week, because I keep my promises!
This is اسبوع.

meanings.note: Takes pronoun suffixes in spoken Jordanian: لأني (because I), لأنك (because you), لأنه (because he/it — also general 'because'), لأنكم (because you pl.).

examples.text: لأنه القهوة الطيبة بتخلي الناس لطاف!
examples.trans: Because good coffee makes people pleasant!
Thank you because you kept the bag safe.

meanings.note: The word 'وفى' (boofi) means 'I keep/fulfill'. It is a common verb in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: شوفوا: راقبوا بريد المكتب الأمامي هالاسبوع، لأني بوفي بوعودي!
examples.trans: Look: Watch your front-desk mail this week, because I keep my promises!
This is وفى.

أصلا.gloss: anyway; in the first place; actually

meanings.en: anyway; in the first place; actually
meanings.note: Everyday conversational adverb meaning 'in the first place / anyway / to begin with'.

examples.trans: Does the attic even have a comfortable bed?
The wire needed adjusting anyway.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببعت, بيبعت).

examples.trans: Last week I sent him a postcard.
She sent a kind thank-you note.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('outside the gate') and standalone ('outside').

examples.trans: It is raining outside.
A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: In Amman, وسط البلد or simply البلد refers to downtown Amman.

examples.trans: We went down to downtown in the morning.
Town is quiet on Friday.

meanings.note: The word 'بلكي' (balki) means 'perhaps'. It is a common adv in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: بلكي المغلف الصغير المختوم بالشمع بجيبتك فيه الجواب يا نور!
examples.trans: Perhaps the small wax-sealed envelope in your pocket has the answer, Nour!
This is بلكي.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوصل, بيوصل).

examples.trans: Our guest arrived right on the second!
An official letter arrived at noon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: رسايل.

examples.trans: An official letter arrived at noon.
We read the letter line by line.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيوت.

examples.trans: The old house has a lovely courtyard.
The neighbourhood houses are built of stone.

meanings.note: The word 'احنا' (iHna) means 'we'. It is a common pron in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أها! شوفوا هالحيط التاريخي الهادي—أكيد احنا بالزبط ورا ساحة الساعة!
examples.trans: Aha! Behold this quiet historic wall—we must be right behind the clock square!
This is احنا.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: طالعة, plural: طالعين).

examples.trans: Count on me, I am heading right out!
We are going up to the third floor.

meanings.note: Common defective verb for walking on foot or things running smoothly.

examples.text: ممنوع تمشي عكاحلك لحد بكرا الصبح.
examples.trans: You mustn't walk on your ankle until tomorrow morning.

examples.text: مشينا عالهدا بالساحة بعد ما وقفت المطر.
examples.trans: We walked gently across the courtyard after the rain stopped.

إلى.gloss: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)

meanings.en: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)
meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: The word 'اللقاء' (اللقاء) means 'اللقاء'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: Goodbye!
This is اللقاء.
